title: Autonomous X-ray mapping reveals previously unseen block-copolymer morphologies, including a nanoscale ladder
summary: An autonomous experiment planner selected synchrotron X-ray measurements across a combinatorial block-copolymer blend sample. The resulting map and targeted electron microscopy revealed previously unreported alternating, skew/bilayer, and ladder-like self-assembled morphologies, and the authors infer a general mechanism of local subdomain partitioning.
ai_technology: gpCAM autonomous experimentation framework for selecting high-value measurements
organization: Brookhaven National Laboratory Center for Functional Nanomaterials and National Synchrotron Light Source II; Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory CAMERA

evidence.tested: An autonomous experiment planner selected synchrotron X-ray measurements across a combinatorial block-copolymer blend sample.
evidence.unknown: The newly discovered results are nanoscale morphologies in one specific polymer-blend/template system; the paper does not show that each morphology is already useful in a device. AI selected measurements, while domain researchers performed electron-microscopy confirmation and interpretation.
evidence.ai_role: The algorithm autonomously chose where to collect synchrotron X-ray scattering data and updated its model online; researchers then used electron microscopy to validate and interpret the novel morphologies.
